races.name: Racing To School Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Louis Veron
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's consistent improver carries Harry Skelton for the first time in this campaign; four wins and places all on Good or Soft, a 13-day turnaround in fine form, and a prominent style that maps perfectly to the dominant pace shape here — likely to be the key market rival to the pace.

runners_data.name: Black Dakota
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and unexposed over hurdles, Robbie David (5) takes over for Daisy Hitchins whose yard has been quiet (0 from 5 in 14 days); recent runs have been over shorter and slower trips, and this step up to 2m2½f Good is an unknown quantity.

runners_data.name: Colibri Bleu
runners_data.note: Unexposed horse from T Ellis carrying a recent form string littered with falls and pulled-ups (FPP-P3); one placed run on Good is the only positive marker, and the erratic jumping record makes confidence difficult to hold regardless of the pace shape.

runners_data.name: Maskarvel
runners_data.note: Jonathan Burke partners this consistent placer who has been placed in five of his last seven runs on similar going; stays in-trip well at 2m2½f and wants to race prominently, making him naturally suited to the race shape that is most likely to unfold.

runners_data.name: McGrath From Clune
runners_data.note: Tom Gretton's veteran (10yo) is a genuine hold-up horse by inclination, though the crowded rear of the field means he is mapped in midfield here — his best chance emerges only if an unexpectedly hot pace causes genuine attrition, which is against the forecast shape; tongue strap worn.

runners_data.name: Penzance
runners_data.note: A long 289-day absence (hurdling debut off a flat campaign) for the John Joseph Hanlon yard which has not struck in 22 runs over 14 days; form is limited to a single hurdle start and a best flat result of 3rd at 10f, making this an intriguing but high-risk unknown.

runners_data.name: Usyk
runners_data.note: Nigel and Willy Twiston-Davies send out this hold-up type who has finished fourth twice at this sort of trip on Good ground; a 7lb claimer (Miss Amber Jackson-Fennell) takes the ride, and the horse needs a faster pace than Take The Boat is likely to set to produce his best from off it.

runners_data.name: Tequila Star
runners_data.note: James Davies partners this 4-year-old who carries a persistent pattern of fading finishes (8-8-9-8-5 in recent form) and comes off a 183-day break; form is exclusively on Flat/AW surfaces and the jumping ability is entirely unproven, with the finish-fade tendency a serious concern.

runners_data.name: Angel Of My Dreams
runners_data.note: Returned 2nd on Good ground last time out for the combined Killahena & McPherson yard, and Nick Slatter (3) claims; a natural hold-up horse by headgear and history, but the field configuration means she is unlikely to settle as far back as she wants — racing out of role reduces her chance in the likely steady-pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Take The Boat
runners_data.note: Harry Bannister's mount for Georgina Nicholls is the race's lone confirmed front-runner and will dictate the fractions; recent hurdle form shows two seconds over longer trips on Good, and while the STYLE_FIT flag tempers the win chance slightly, controlling the pace from the front on this flat track remains a genuine threat.

races.paceDynamic: Take The Boat is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger likely to press them hard, Harry Bannister can dictate a measured, sustainable gallop from the outset on the 2m2½f Good-ground Stratford circuit. Louis Veron and Maskarvel will want to race prominently and may track Take The Boat closely, creating a small cluster at the head of affairs rather than a true lone leader, but the overall tempo is unlikely to be searingly fast. The hold-up contingent — Penzance, Usyk, Tequila Star — will have ground to make up off a steady pace, and both Angel Of My Dreams and McGrath From Clune, though natural hold-up horses, have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear of the field is overcrowded with their type; neither is expected to secure their preferred position in this shape. A controlled, honest pace with a prominent-racing winner is the dominant outcome here — horses who can travel just off the leader and quicken from the second-last hurdle are best placed, while closers from further back face a stiff task if the race is not run at a searching enough clip to bring them into it late.

watchPoints.text: Take The Boat sets the fractions uncontested — if Harry Bannister finds an unchallenged lead and the pace stays honest rather than dawdling, watch whether Louis Veron has the cruising speed to close the gap from two out.

Tequila Star's jumping is entirely unknown — a 183-day absence combined with a persistent finish-fade pattern and no hurdles experience could make this horse a safety risk early in the race, particularly in a field of 10 at a tight circuit like Stratford.

McGrath From Clune and Angel Of My Dreams may both attempt to sit closer than their natural style allows given the crowded rear; if they do, the midfield becomes congested and contact or interference at the hurdles is a realistic possibility.

Penzance represents a significant step into the unknown — 289 days off, moving from flat to hurdles, for a trainer who has not won in 22 starts over the past fortnight; monitor market moves and watch closely in the paddock for signs of fitness.

Maskarvel's trainer Alastair Ralph also shows 0 from 5 in the 14-day window, but the horse's consistent placed record (four times in seven Good-ground runs) means a clean round could bring him into play late if the prominent runners trade blows from the second-last.

races.name: Stratford Supporting Racing Staff Week Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Buxted Reel
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner who sets up the entire race shape; Tom Lacey's seven-year-old has a 1/8 trainer 14-day record suggesting stable in reasonable form, ran only 27 days ago at Goodwood in testing ground, and the step back to a right-handed turning track suits a horse that dictates from the front — though a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 reminds us this is technically out of their optimal role, so watch if rivals crowd them early.

runners_data.name: Dublinofficecallin
runners_data.note: Kerry Lee's five-year-old landed a course-and-distance win over 2m on Good going last time, recording the only win in this field in similar conditions (1W1P in sim-going); Connor O'Farrell takes the ride and the horse's hold-up style means everything depends on Buxted Reel stretching things enough to bring them off the pace.

runners_data.name: Mayday Games
runners_data.note: Sharply out of form and returning from a 254-day absence, with a worrying pattern of finishing positions (PP/F0) and a tagged tendency to fade in the finish; Shaun Lycett has a 0/5 strike rate over the 14-day window and this hold-up type will need a fast gallop to be seen to best advantage — the layoff and form make this a difficult one to support.

runners_data.name: Giddyupadingdong
runners_data.note: Neil Mulholland's six-year-old boasts a win on Good ground (1W1P in sim-going across three qualifying runs), is freshened up on just 23 days, and wears a tongue-tie for the first time — Bradley Harris claims 3lb and the horse's hold-up profile sits comfortably within the expected race shape if the pace is genuine.

runners_data.name: Estate Planning
runners_data.note: Bernard Llewellyn's five-year-old has run exclusively on soft ground in all five recent starts (0W2P in sim-going), making this return to Good ground a notable query; a 132-day absence compounds the concern, and while Ben Jones is an able pilot the form figures (68405) don't inspire confidence in this trip or surface.

runners_data.name: Hellion
runners_data.note: Donald McCain's four-year-old has a genuinely hold-up profile but the redistribution note signals it is unlikely to achieve its natural position in this race; prior form shows a single placed run from five starts (mostly on soft) and a 61-day break, plus first-time headgear (p) — the horse is a fresh entity today but the modest form ceiling limits realistic expectations.

runners_data.name: Papa Oscar
runners_data.note: Clare Hobson's four-year-old is a natural hold-up type pushed into a midfield slot by the density of similar runners — headgear (h) worn throughout recent starts and a 39-day gap since last run; sim-going form of 0W0P across three Good-ground starts tells its own story and the step up in trip from 8f flat runs at Stanningly is a considerable ask.

runners_data.name: Northern Rose
runners_data.note: Gary Hanmer's six-year-old is the most interesting hold-up type in the field by form — four placed efforts in 14 Good-ground starts including two seconds — but returns from a 241-day absence and has the longest layoff bar Mayday Games; headgear (tp) is routine, James Davies rides, and a full return to fitness would make this one interesting at the right price.

runners_data.name: Kotgar
runners_data.note: Mrs C Williams's five-year-old wears headgear (p) and contests Good ground competently (6 runs, 0W1P in sim-going), but finishing positions of 647P5 show a horse that struggles to land a blow; an 83-day break is a mild concern and the redistribution means its true hold-up style is compromised by the likely race shape.

runners_data.name: Cosmic Spirit
runners_data.note: Ben Case's four-year-old is tagged with a fade-in-finish flag and a 117-day absence, which is a concerning combination for a horse placed in a notional midfield slot but naturally preferring to be held up; an amateur rider claiming 7lb (Mr Joseph Stevenson) adds to the risk profile and sim-going form of 0W0P across seven equivalent runs underlines the difficulty.

runners_data.name: Hopjes
runners_data.note: Harriet Dickin's six-year-old wore a tongue-tie in recent starts and went 9/11 on Good ground at the course last time from 14 sim-going runs (0W0P); back after 25 days which at least means fitness is not a concern, but the redistribution of this genuine hold-up horse into a midfield slot, combined with a low OR of 69, limits the upside significantly.

runners_data.name: Pink Walls
runners_data.note: Michael Mullineaux's six-year-old wears headgear (h) and has a form string of P0-P — non-completions are a jumping concern over hurdles; just 39 days since last run and Kevin Brogan takes the ride, but 0W0P across 12 Good-ground starts is a deeply uninspiring record and this natural hold-up type racing out of position further diminishes its chance.

races.paceDynamic: Buxted Reel is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner novice handicap hurdle and, with no natural challenger identified to press them through the early stages, they are highly likely to control the tempo from the front at Stratford's tight track over 2m½f on Good ground. The overwhelming bulk of this field — Dublinofficecallin, Mayday Games, Giddyupadingdong, Estate Planning, and a cluster of redistributed hold-up types — are genuine closers who will race in behind and rely on a strong enough gallop being set to bring them into play. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the map can place at the rear; Hellion, Papa Oscar, Northern Rose, Kotgar, Cosmic Spirit, Hopjes, and Pink Walls are all true hold-up horses who have been pushed into midfield positions on the map purely because there is insufficient space behind — none of them should be assumed to secure a genuine sit-and-sprint role. This race shape — a single, uncontested front-runner on Good ground at a turning track — strongly favours horses with the tactical versatility to race prominently or in the first half of the field and sustain their effort through the final bend, rather than horses needing a searching gallop to close into from off the pace.

watchPoints.text: Buxted Reel's early manoeuvres are the key to the entire race — if any of the redistributed hold-up horses (particularly Hellion or Papa Oscar) push forward aggressively at the start and crowd Buxted Reel, the gallop could quicken unpredictably and undermine the controlled-pace scenario the map favours.

Northern Rose returns from a 241-day absence but holds the most consistent placed form on Good ground in this field — watch for early signs of ring-rustiness in the paddock and opening stages, as a fully fit version of this horse would make it a genuine contender in most scenarios.

Mayday Games and Cosmic Spirit both carry a fade-in-finish flag alongside lengthy layoffs (254 and 117 days respectively); if either jumps poorly or drops away from the pack early, they could present an interference risk at the rear of a compressed field.

Several horses wearing headgear for the first time or returning to it (Giddyupadingdong tongue-tie, Hellion p, Pink Walls h) — behavioural changes in the early stages at a tight track like Stratford could affect position and are worth monitoring as the field settles after the first hurdle.

The amateur rider on Cosmic Spirit (Mr Joseph Stevenson, 7lb claim) is worth noting in a race where the pace shape is already compressed — inexperienced handling of a hold-up type forced into an unnatural midfield position could lead to interference or position loss on Stratford's sharp bends.

races.name: Karen Poulter Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Seeyouinmydreams
runners_data.note: Jack Andrews in the saddle for a yard running at 2/8 over 14 days; five wins and ten places from 15 similar-going runs tells a consistent Good-ground story, and the hg:ht headgear is retained — the lone front-runner owns the race shape here but the STYLE_FIT flag notes he's operating slightly outside his optimal profile.

runners_data.name: Nibras Gold
runners_data.note: Jonathan Burke partners a horse with two wins and eight places from 13 Good-ground starts — an outstanding strike rate — and the hg:p headgear is unchanged; sits naturally prominent and has the profile to track Seeyouinmydreams closely and wear him down from two out.

runners_data.name: In The Air
runners_data.note: Trainer Alastair Ralph sends this one out just 17 days after its last run with a T14 figure of 0/5 suggesting the yard is quiet, but the horse itself carries five wins from similar-going runs and won at 21f last time — the step back in trip to 2m1f at sharp Stratford may catch him out slightly.

runners_data.name: Not So Sobers
runners_data.note: David Bass takes the ride on a seven-year-old whose last two runs both produced wins on Good ground at 16f, but the 42-day absence and a suspicious hg:h headgear entry combined with a history of very poor runs (10th, 6th) on shorter/faster tracks adds risk; needs the gallop to strengthen late to suit his genuine hold-up profile.

runners_data.name: Whatyouwaitingfor
runners_data.note: Gavin Sheehan rides a five-year-old with a solid recent form string of 1223-3 and Good-ground competence, but this horse is a natural prominent type pushed into a midfield mapping because Seeyouinmydreams claims the front; the STYLE_FIT flag applies and its true chance is reliant on getting closer to the pace than the race shape easily allows.

runners_data.name: Lheur De Gloire
runners_data.note: Ben Pauling's five-year-old won last time out 19 days ago and has hg:t headgear, but its Good-ground record of just 3 wins from 7 similar-going runs is modest; like Whatyouwaitingfor, it is a genuine front-runner displaced to midfield in this mapping — its best form comes when dictating, which it cannot easily do here.

runners_data.name: Boom Boom
runners_data.note: Rob Summers sends this eight-year-old out 17 days after its last run with a T14 figure of 0/1, and the recent form string of 187P-P includes two pulls-up which raise jumping reliability concerns; does hold two Good-ground wins at 20f+ but the sharp 2m1f Stratford trip looks short for a hold-up horse needing time to warm into a race.

races.paceDynamic: Seeyouinmydreams is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no natural pace rival to pressure him, he should bowl along at a controlled, manageable gallop on Good ground at Stratford — a flat, sharp right-handed track that strongly rewards those who travel prominently and jump fluently. Nibras Gold and In The Air will look to sit just behind him and hunt him down from the home turn, creating a compact, tactical chase where the premium is on jumping and quick acceleration rather than raw stamina. The field actually contains more genuine prominent-minded horses than can all occupy their preferred berths — Whatyouwaitingfor and Lheur De Gloire are natural front-runners who have been mapped to midfield simply because Seeyouinmydreams owns that position, and they are unlikely to replicate the dominance their form suggests when racing out of their natural role. This race shape — a single uncontested leader, steady honest gallop, sharp track — strongly favours the prominent-to-midfield stalkers who can track the pace, jump cleanly, and quicken off the final bend rather than hold-up horses who need a strong, searching gallop to bring them into it late.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Whatyouwaitingfor or Lheur De Gloire attempt to push forward at the start — if either forces their way up to track Seeyouinmydreams, the pace dynamic shifts immediately and the tempo could rise sharply, altering every scenario probability.

Boom Boom has pulled up twice in recent starts; monitor his jumping in the early stages — a mistake or refusal at a fence would directly affect the safety of the race and could cause interference for horses racing close behind.

Not So Sobers has a 42-day absence and an hg:h headgear entry that does not appear in recent outings — if this is a new application it can sharpen a hold-up horse unpredictably and he may race more keenly than his style profile suggests.

In The Air's trainer T14 figure of 0/5 is worth noting — Alastair Ralph's yard appears to be in a quiet spell, and while the horse's own form is strong, a yard out of form at a quick turnaround of 17 days is a mild flag on confidence.

races.name: Clear Insurance Management Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Machete Beach
runners_data.note: A 5-year-old in excellent recent form — two wins from last four starts on Good ground — ridden by Gavin Sheehan for the in-form Jamie Snowden yard (4/9 over 14 days); the style-fit tag notes it races slightly out of strict role here, but in a three-runner field where it meets no pace opposition whatsoever that caveat carries little weight.

runners_data.name: Hooper
runners_data.note: A veteran hold-up mare aged 10 whose best recent form has come at longer trips on softer ground; headgear (t) worn, and a 37-day absence plus that pulled-up run last time are negative flags, while a 7lb claim from Miss Amber Jackson-Fennell offers partial compensation for what looks a stiff task.

runners_data.name: Edelak
runners_data.note: A lightly-raced 4-year-old with back-to-back wins earlier in 2024, now ridden by Harry Skelton for the Skelton stable operating at a 16/31 clip in the last fortnight; pea-green headgear (p) worn, 28 days between runs is acceptable, and a natural prominent style means the horse is perfectly placed to apply second-flight pressure if needed.

races.paceDynamic: Machete Beach is the lone confirmed pace-setter in this three-runner field and will stride to the front unchallenged from the outset, setting a sustainable rhythm over 2m½f on Good turf at Stratford. Edelak, also a prominent-style runner, will likely tuck in directly behind rather than contest the lead, while Hooper — a hold-up type — will bring up the rear from the off, likely last of three for much of the race. With no pressure on the leader and only two pursuers, Machete Beach controls the tempo entirely, dictating a measured gallop that plays to stamina and jumping fluency rather than raw finishing speed. This shape strongly favours either the front-runner who dictates and jumps well or a prominent horse with a turn of foot who can pounce approaching the last, making Machete Beach and Edelak the principal tactical beneficiaries.

watchPoints.text: Machete Beach's jumping accuracy is the pivotal variable — a clean round at Good-ground Stratford seals the race shape, but any error at a flight could instantly change the dynamic in a field of only three.

Edelak's headgear (p) is noted on what is likely a first-time or early use; if it sharpens the horse's jumping or freshness it could manufacture a more forceful challenge than the pace map currently implies.
Hooper's pulled-up run last time out and the step back in trip from 20f+ to 2m½f raises a fitness and suitability question — watch in the paddock for any signs of her condition before the off.

With only three runners, non-completion by any horse dramatically reshapes the contest; check market moves close to post time as any late scratching or market drift could signal connections' concerns.

races.name: Happy 80th Birthday David Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Tamarind Bay
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with Sean Bowen taking a notable booking for Mickey Bowen's yard; five recent runs all on soft-or-firm ground softer than today suggests Good is the best surface seen for a while, though sim-going record shows 0 wins from 3 placed efforts — needs the pace to be strong enough to make late ground count over 2m6½f.

runners_data.name: Harrys Hope
runners_data.note: Lone front-runner with a clear form profile of making the running (3 wins from 8 similar-going runs); the critical flag here is 235 days off since last run with Ben Pauling having just 1 runner from 7 in the past fortnight — fitness on return from a long absence over a stamina trip is the primary risk, though the controlled pace he sets may mask any rustiness.

runners_data.name: Two To Tango
runners_data.note: Active and in form (ran 17 days ago, second last time), Emma Lavelle's charge has an outstanding 13 from 15 record on Good going and handles this trip well; the hood (headgear) is a retained positive, and prominent racing style means Two To Tango should naturally slot into a close-tracking role behind Harrys Hope where the race shape does the work.

runners_data.name: Mix Of Clover
runners_data.note: Strong recent form on Good ground (3 wins, 8 placed from 15 similar-going runs) and Tom Broughton claims 3lb for this veteran chaser — however, with multiple prominent types in the field, Mix Of Clover is a natural front-runner who will likely find himself unable to press forward as freely as he would prefer, racing in a slightly unfamiliar position with a style-fit discount attached.

runners_data.name: Grillon De Monty
runners_data.note: Won over 23f on Good ground and showed placed form 30 days ago, but at age 11 and with Lewis Stones claiming 3lb, this is a modest profile; a genuine prominent racer by nature, Grillon De Monty is the most likely of the redistributed pair to be squeezed widest from his preferred position, and the trainer has had zero runners in the past fortnight — limited angle here.

races.paceDynamic: Harrys Hope is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with just five runners over 2m6½f on Good ground at Stratford, will be able to stride into a comfortable lead from the outset without any genuine pressure from rivals. Two To Tango and Mix Of Clover are both natural prominent types who will push forward to track Harrys Hope, though with more prominent runners than the race shape can comfortably accommodate, Mix Of Clover and Grillon De Monty are unlikely to fully secure their preferred positions and may find themselves racing slightly further back than ideal. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all get their position — Harrys Hope and Two To Tango are most likely to actually secure the lead bracket, with Mix Of Clover and Grillon De Monty squeezed into a less familiar midfield role. This race shape strongly favours a horse that can sit close to a controlled, unhurried pace and travel — the prominent-to-mid profile suits best, and any horse that can settle within striking range of Harrys Hope's predictable gallop before the home straight holds the clearest tactical advantage.

watchPoints.text: Harrys Hope's jumping must be monitored from the outset — 235 days off racing means any hesitancy or jumping errors at the first few fences could unravel the entire pace map and leave the race leaderless.
Mix Of Clover and Grillon De Monty may jostle for position on the first bend as both want to race prominently — watch for crowding behind Harrys Hope that could unsettle the early order.

Two To Tango's headgear and recent racecourse fitness (17 days since last run) make it the most dangerous challenger if Harrys Hope's stamina flags on the long run from the last — watch for Lavelle's runner looming up at the third-last.

Tamarind Bay's Sean Bowen booking is a market pointer worth noting — if Bowen has been specifically engaged for a hold-up horse in a small field where the pace may not be strong, that is tactically ambitious and worth factoring into pricing.
Good ground is confirmed for all six races at Stratford today with no variance — no going softening or firming concern to reassess at the off.

runners_data.name: Hiconic
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type who has shown consistent placed form over 16f-19f in good to similar conditions, and his course form at Stratford (two runs) is a tangible positive in a race that lacks pace — 33 days since last run is standard, and tongue strap is noted but not a worry on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Saint Polo
runners_data.note: Has placed form over 20f and 24f in good ground, suggesting stamina is not the limiting factor, and Luke Scott (3lb claimer) is a relevant booking for a trainer with two winners from twenty runners in the last fortnight — although his natural rear-of-field style may see him pushed forward by the tactical vacuum, diluting the full advantage of his staying profile.

runners_data.name: Backer Bilk
runners_data.note: A lightly-raced four-year-old who has back-to-back placed finishes over 16f on good ground and is bred for this kind of test; trained by the McPherson/Killahena partnership who are 3/9 in 14 days, which is a live form pointer — his natural instinct to settle may see him drawn into a prominent role by default in this pace-less field, slightly compromising his ideal ride.

runners_data.name: Ocean Heights
runners_data.note: David Pipe's runner arrives 20 days fresh with a recent third over 18f in good going as a confidence-builder, and the combination of visor and tongue strap (headgear unchanged) suggests he needs to be kept focused — a true hold-up horse who ends up in a midfield berth by necessity rather than design, but his best efforts over similar trips suggest he handles this kind of test when everything clicks.

runners_data.name: Raffles Nobu
runners_data.note: Only five days since his last run is the immediate flag here — he was placed over 20f in good going recently and has placed form in similar conditions, but back-to-back runs in quick succession for a seven-pound claimer in a race with no natural pace could be demanding; a genuine hold-up horse pushed forward by race shape, his chance is real if fresh enough.

runners_data.name: Stay In The Game
runners_data.note: The most recent winner in the field (1/16f/GOO in last five runs) and has a trio of placed finishes over 16f in good ground — John Joseph Hanlon's runner arrives just three days after a start, which is worth monitoring, but his OR of 104 gives him a class edge and his sharp recent form over this course configuration is the headline angle.

races.paceDynamic: With every single runner in this six-horse field carrying a hold-up profile, there is no confirmed front-runner and no horse with any natural inclination to force the pace — this race is almost certain to crawl into a sprint finish from the home turn. The field will likely dawdle through the early stages, with runners jockeying for position without any genuine pace anchor, before the tempo suddenly lifts in the straight and it becomes a stamina-and-finishing-kick scramble over the final two furlongs. Stay In The Game, with a recent course win over 2m and a sharp recent record at 16f, and Hiconic, a confirmed hold-up type with decent recent form over this trip in similar going, are best-equipped for a late-surge scenario. The race shape overwhelmingly favours hold-up closers with a sharp turn of foot in the straight, since nobody will be softened up by a genuine gallop — the premium is on jumping fluently and arriving late with a kick. The field holds more hold-up types than can realistically all settle at the rear; Saint Polo, Backer Bilk, Raffles Nobu, and Ocean Heights are all natural hold-up horses redistributed forward on the map, and in practice the jockeys with the most confidence or the most forcing instructions — most likely Saint Polo's Luke Scott or Backer Bilk's Nick Slatter — are likely to end up prominent simply because someone must fill the vacuum at the head of affairs.

watchPoints.text: Stay In The Game runs just three days after his last start — monitor any market drift or firmness at the off as a guide to whether connections are confident he has bounced back fully.

With no genuine front-runner, watch which jockey takes up the lead in the early stages — whoever is pushed to the front by default (likely Saint Polo or Backer Bilk) will be racing completely against their natural style and may fade sharply from the home turn.
Raffles Nobu returns only five days after his previous run under a 7lb claiming rider — a quick turnaround for a horse who relies on freshness to produce his best finishing effort.

Backer Bilk is the youngest runner in the field at four years old in a race full of experienced older horses — watch whether Nick Slatter can settle him early given the likely crawling gallop, as greenness could see him waste energy.

Ocean Heights has the most recent course experience in similar conditions and jumps with visor fitted — if the race develops into a messy sprint finish, clean jumping at the last two hurdles will be the deciding factor for all six runners and he is one to note if the race flows his way.
